title: Review Virtual Keyboard native libraries packaged in the Android APK
scope: Packaging review candidate discovered during DEV-004; investigation and any deployment change are deferred. No runtime keyboard defect is established.
finding: Android APKs contain the Qt Virtual Keyboard native library and platform input-context plugin even though the app's desktop keyboard loader is disabled and its QML module has no Virtual Keyboard dependency.
evidence: The existing dist/QShopper-x86_64-debug.apk and fresh out/dev004/android-x86 APK both contain libQt6VirtualKeyboard_x86_64.so (466304 bytes) and libplugins_platforminputcontexts_qtvirtualkeyboardplugin_x86_64.so (14496 bytes). Their contents are byte-identical between those APKs.
The previous ARM64 APK also contains the corresponding native libraries.

The fresh Android build explicitly requests QSHOPPER_DESKTOP_KEYBOARD=ON to verify the platform override: the generated loader source is empty and qmldir has no Virtual Keyboard dependency. This preserves the runtime native-keyboard configuration.
An initial package audit assumed these files should be absent; baseline comparison showed the payload predates DEV-004. Treat this as a packaging investigation, not a new build-cleanup regression.
expected: Determine whether the native payload is required by Qt deployment or can be excluded cleanly while retaining Android's system IME and the desktop development keyboard.
implementation_notes: Trace androiddeployqt, QML import scanning and platform-input-context plugin dependencies before identifying a cause; no particular scanner or source file is proven responsible.
Keep any supported exclusion KISS and confined to Android. Avoid post-build deletion workarounds without establishing the actual dependency chain.

Characterize the intended deployment contract before treating library presence as a bug. If removing it is appropriate, add a repeatable APK-content check and verify fresh packages for both shipped ABIs.
Verify real Gboard entry, retained keyboard on Return, hide/reopen and native Back with isolated emulator data; keep desktop keyboard builds/tests working.
Coordinate the actual shipped-dependency inventory with release preparation and About notices.
acceptance_criteria: Document the dependency path and decide whether the libraries are required or unnecessary payload.
If an exclusion is justified, implement it separately with package-content and native-IME verification; otherwise document why the payload remains.

ui023_payload_observation.finding: Fresh UI-023 Android packages still contain Canvas2D and CanvasPainter libraries despite removal of explicit QML/module/link usage. Inventory the actual APK; the deployment dependency/scan path has not been established. No packaging change is included in UI-023.
